_comment: Acknowledged-warning ledger (v3.28 zero-warning discipline). Each record silences exactly one check_run.py WARN that the weekly quality audit reviewed and judged unfixable without falsifying immutable history (run records are never edited after their fire; entries are immutable). warn() reclassifies a warning as ACK when record.check equals the check label and record.match is a substring of the message — pin `match` to the specific run/subject so nothing else is ever swallowed. Only the weekly quality audit (or an operator-directed session) adds records, never a run for its own fresh warnings; every addition names its reason and date and appears in the commit diff for review.

Reviewed by the 2026-07-26 weekly quality audit and judged unfixable: every Sonnet (cti-verification-alt) spawn in that fire terminated on the content-safety classifier — iteration 2 was retried and failed again, as did three of four research spawns — so no other-model confirmation pass was available. The run recorded the blocked-spawn exception in verification.confirmation_waived exactly as the policy requires, and both confirming iterations were genuine independent CLEAN passes; only the two-DIFFERENT-models requirement was waived. The record is immutable, so nothing can change it. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: teaching check_run.py to auto-pass a same-model confirmation whenever confirmation_waived is non-null would let any future run silence the rotation check by writing its own waiver text, which is the self-serve mute button the discipline forbids and a weakening of hard invariant #11. The warning did its job — it surfaced for review, and this ledger record is the review.
